Comprehension – C1 Answer the following (p. 6)
1. Where were Lucy and Nithin going?
Lucy and Nithin were returning home from school.
2. What did they see?
They saw a man walking with his pet dog, trying to talk to the dog.
3. Why were the animals attracted towards Maharshi?
Because he loved animals and birds and spoke to them just as he would speak with people.
4. Where did Ramana Maharshi keep the animals?
He kept the animals in his ashram.
5. What happened one day when he was sitting by the hillside?
A snake crawled over his legs. He did not move or show any fear.
6. How did he feed the peacocks?
He called the peacocks by making sounds of their cries, and they came and ate peanuts, rice and mangoes from his hands.
7. Why did Ramana Maharshi not allow anyone to kill snakes?
Because the snakes do not trouble us. We have come to their home, so we have no right to trouble them.
8. Who told stories to Lucy?
Lucy's grandmother told her stories.
Comprehension – C2 Discuss with your friends and answer in four to six sentences each (p. 6)
1. Describe Ramana Maharshi's love for animals.

Ramana Maharshi loved animals and birds very much. He fed the animals and birds first and ate only after feeding them. He called the dogs 'boys' and his cow 'Lakshmi'. Animals and birds came to him and ate peanuts, rice and mangoes from his hands.
2. What did Ramana Maharshi say about killing of snakes?
Ramana Maharshi never allowed people to kill snakes in his ashram. He said that we have come to the snakes' home and have no right to trouble them. He also said that they do not trouble us.

Vocabulary – V2 State whether the statements are true (T) or false (F); correct the false ones (p. 17)
1. Damon and Pythias were lovers of truth.
T
2. Dionysius was a kind ruler.
F. Dionysius was an evil-minded ruler.
3. Damon wanted to settle his family affairs before he died.
F. It was Pythias who wanted to settle his family affairs (meet his mother and sister) before he died.
4. The king was sure that Pythias would return.
F. The king was certain that Pythias would not return.
5. Damon was ready to die for his friend.
T
6. Pythias reached in time to save his friend.
F. Pythias did not return in time on the fixed day, but he came back later and offered to be punished.
Comprehension – C1 Answer the following questions (p. 18)
1. Where did Damon and Pythias live?
Damon and Pythias lived in the city of Syracuse.
2. Who was the ruler of Syracuse?
King Dionysius was the ruler of Syracuse.
3. Why did the king want to punish Pythias?
Pythias had called the king cruel and had said something against him, so the king became very angry.
4. What did Pythias wish to fulfil before he died?
He wished to meet his old mother and sister, arrange his sister's marriage and bid goodbye to his mother.
5. What was the condition laid down by the king?
The king fixed the day and hour of Pythias' return. If he did not return in time, Damon would have to die instead of him.
6. Why was Pythias delayed while returning?
He had to face many dangers on the way, so he was delayed.
7. What did both the friends argue over?
Both of them argued about who should be punished. Each one asked the king to hang him instead of the other.
8. Why did the king set both of them free?
The king had never seen such friendship. Both of them had kept their promises, so the king set both of them free.
Comprehension – C2 Discuss with your friends and answer in four to six sentences each (p. 18)
1. How do you know that Damon and Pythias were good friends? Give some examples from the story.

Damon and Pythias were true friends. Pythias went to meet his mother and sister and then returned to save Damon. Damon trusted Pythias and said that he would keep his promise. Even when Pythias was late, Damon was ready to die in his place because he loved him dearly. Both of them kept their promises.
2. What made the king change his decision at the end?

The king was surprised to see Pythias come back on his own, even after facing many dangers. Both friends argued to take the punishment for each other. The king had never seen such friendship in his life. He was impressed by their loyalty and set both of them free.

qb.q: What happened when Pythias returned on time?
qb.a: Pythias returned just in time to face his punishment. The king was surprised, was touched by their true friendship and decided to forgive both of them.

qb.q: What does the story teach us about friendship?
qb.a: The story teaches that real friendship means being loyal, truthful and ready to make sacrifices for each other.

qb.q: Why did the king agree to let Pythias go home?

qb.q: What shows that Damon trusted Pythias completely?
qb.a: Damon stayed in prison willingly, knowing he could be punished if Pythias did not return. This showed that he had full trust in his friend’s promise.

qb.q: How did Pythias prove that he was a true friend?
qb.a: Pythias returned on time, even though he could have escaped. He kept his promise to save Damon, proving his loyalty and friendship.

qb.q: What did the king learn from Damon and Pythias?
qb.a: The king learned that true friendship is valuable and rare. He realised that love and trust are more powerful than fear and punishment.

qb.q: Describe the character of the king in the beginning and end of the story.
qb.a: In the beginning, the king was cruel and strict. By the end of the story, he became kind and forgiving after witnessing the strong bond of friendship between Damon and Pythias.

Comprehension – C1 Answer the following questions in two or three sentences each (p. 31)
1. Where did Prem and his family live?
Prem and his family lived in a small village near Bandipur forest.
2. Why was Prem sad?
Prem was sad because he had heard that many trees in the forest would be cut down. He wondered where the animals and birds would go.
3. What did Prem and his friend Nasrin do to solve the problem?
They went to the forest and found out what was happening. They decided to approach the authorities to stop the cutting down of trees, and Prem wrote a letter to the President of Gramsabha.
4. Whom did they write the letter to?
They wrote the letter to the President of Gramsabha.
5. What was the complaint about?
The complaint was about the cutting down of trees in the forest.
6. Who signed the complaint?
Prem's parents, their friends, people in the local community and people of nearby villages signed the complaint.
7. What did the President of Gramsabha write back to Prem?
The President of Gramsabha wrote that Prem's request was accepted and that the trees in the forest would not be cut down. The plants, animals and birds would be safe.
Comprehension – C2 Discuss with your friends and answer in four to six sentences each (p. 31)
1. Describe Prem's love for the forest and the animals.

Prem loved trees, birds, animals and flowers. He took an evening walk in the forest every day. He became friendly with the animals and birds there. When he heard that the trees would be cut, he was very sad. He wanted to protect the forest and its animals, so he took action.
2. How did the President of Gramsabha praise Prem?
The President of Gramsabha wrote that they were happy about the love Prem had shown towards nature. She said his request had been accepted and the trees would not be cut down.
3. What do you learn from this lesson?
We learn that we should love and protect nature, trees, animals and birds. Even children can make a difference by acting together and speaking up for what is right.

qb.q: Write a character sketch of Prem.

qb.q: Write a character sketch of Nasrin.
qb.a: Nasrin is Prem’s loyal and supportive friend. She stands by him and helps him take action to protect the forest. Her helpful nature, concern for the environment and calm thinking make her a dependable companion in the story.

qb.q: Write a character sketch of Prem’s mother.
qb.a: Prem’s mother is caring, understanding and wise. She listens to her son’s concern and guides him to take constructive action by advising him to write to the President of the Gramasabha. Her support plays an important role in encouraging Prem to act responsibly.

qb.q: Write a character sketch of Heera the deer.
qb.a: Heera is a gentle forest animal and a friend of Prem. She appears worried and scared after hearing about the trees being cut, showing how deeply animals are affected by human actions. Her emotional response highlights the importance of protecting wildlife.

qb.q: Write a character sketch of the President of the Gramasabha.
qb.a: The President of the Gramasabha is a kind and responsible leader. He respects the voices of young citizens like Prem and values the preservation of nature. His quick and positive response to Prem’s letter shows his willingness to take action for the community’s good.

qb.q: How do Prem and Nasrin show teamwork and care for nature?
qb.a: Prem and Nasrin work together with dedication to protect the forest. They discuss the issue, support each other and involve the community in a peaceful way. Their teamwork shows friendship, leadership and a shared love for the environment.

qb.q: What is the role of nature in the story of Prem?
qb.a: In the story, nature plays a crucial role as Prem’s deep connection with the forest, animals and trees drives the story. The forest represents life and harmony. Prem’s concern for its possible destruction shows how deeply he values nature and teaches readers the importance of protecting it.

qb.q: How does Prem show his responsibility towards the environment?
qb.a: Prem shows his responsibility towards the environment when he learns about the possible tree-cutting in the forest. He does not ignore the problem. He discusses it with his friend Nasrin and writes a letter to the President of the Gramasabha, showing his maturity and leadership in caring for nature.

qb.q: What qualities of Prem’s mother make her a wise and caring parent?
qb.a: Prem’s mother shows wisdom and care by listening to her son’s concerns and guiding him towards a positive solution. She advises him to take responsible action and write a letter to the President of the Gramasabha, helping him address the issue calmly and effectively.

qb.q: How did the villagers contribute to Prem’s cause?
qb.a: The villagers contributed to Prem’s cause by signing the letter he wrote to the President of the Gramasabha. Their support, along with that of nearby villagers, showed their collective concern for the environment and helped Prem save the forest.

qb.q: Why was the President of the Gramasabha’s decision important?
qb.a: The President’s decision to stop the cutting of trees was important because it showed how a responsible leader can make a significant impact on protecting nature. His positive response reflected his commitment to preserving the environment for future generations.

Why did the speaker feel emotionally connected to the tamarind tree?
qb.a: The tamarind tree gave the speaker fruit, shade and a peaceful place to rest. It symbolised home, comfort and happy memories, which made it deeply personal.

qb.q: How does the speaker describe their experience under the tamarind tree?
qb.a: The speaker felt joy and peace under the tree. They often rested in its shade and admired the distant hills with laughter and a smile.

qb.q: How does the poet use imagery to describe the tamarind tree and its surroundings?
qb.a: The poet uses images like “shady boughs”, “distant blue hills” and “winding lane” to create a peaceful and nostalgic atmosphere around the tree.

qb.q: What change does the speaker observe on returning to the tree’s location?
qb.a: The speaker finds that the tree is gone, having been “ripped apart”, and only an “empty hole” remains where it once stood.

qb.q: What does the “empty hole” at the end of the poem symbolise?
qb.a: The “empty hole” symbolises loss, emotional emptiness and the absence of something deeply cherished and irreplaceable.

qb.q: How does the tone of the poem shift from beginning to end?

qb.q: Explain the significance of the line “That magnificent tree, that was my life.”

qb.q: What emotions are conveyed in the line “My eyes filled with tears”?
qb.a: This line expresses deep sorrow, grief and a sense of irreparable loss as the speaker mourns the absence of the tamarind tree.

qb.q: What is the message or moral of the poem?
qb.a: The poem shows the importance of memory, the deep emotional bond people have with nature and the pain of irreversible loss. It reminds us to value the things that bring us peace and comfort, because they may not last forever. It urges readers to appreciate and protect what they love before it is gone.

qb.q: How does the speaker show their connection to nature in the poem?
qb.a: The speaker’s bond with the tamarind tree reveals a deep connection to nature. They see the tree as part of their life, describing it as “magnificent” and central to their identity. This connection is personal, emotional and full of love and respect for the natural world.

lessons.notes: Prose: The Boss Who Cares (p. 37–42). Poem: Believe (p. 45–46).

With the help of your teacher, find out what work has been done in ISRO and DRDO.

Comprehension – C1 Answer the following questions in a sentence or two each (p. 41–42)
1. How many scientists were there at Thumba Space Centre?
There were about seventy scientists at Thumba Space Centre.
2. What made them restless?
There was so much work, and the work was adventurous and took a lot of time. It made them restless.
3. Where did one of the scientists want to take his children?
He wanted to take his children to the exhibition in town.
4. At what time was he permitted to leave?
He was permitted to leave the office at half past five in the evening.
5. When did the scientist leave the office?
He left the office at half past eight in the evening.
6. How did his wife react when he entered the house?
She did not scold him. She calmly asked him whether he would like coffee or dinner.
7. What did she ask him?
She asked him whether he would like a cup of coffee, or whether she should serve dinner if he was hungry.
8. Where were the children?
The children were not at home. They had gone to the exhibition.
9. Who had taken them to the exhibition?
The boss had taken them to the exhibition.
10. Who was the boss?
The boss was Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
Comprehension – C2 Discuss with your friends and answer in five to six sentences each (p. 42)
1. What do you understand by '...it took a lot of time'? Explain.

It means the work on rockets was difficult and needed a lot of time to finish. The scientists had to work from morning till night and sometimes went home at midnight. The task was adventurous, so it took a long time to complete.
2. What do you think the scientist thought on the way back home?
He remembered the promise he had made to his children and felt sad for disappointing them. He wondered how he would calm his wife. He felt that he had let his family down.
3. When the scientist returned home, his wife was very calm. The scientist did not expect this. Why?
He expected his wife to scold him for being late. But she was calm because she knew that the boss had come at quarter past five and taken the children to the exhibition.
4. What do you want to say about the boss?

The boss was kind, caring and understanding. He cared for his employees and their families. He allowed the scientist to leave early and took the children to the exhibition himself. ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.

qb.a: The scientists were involved in developing rockets, which was an adventurous and challenging task. The workload was intense, which made them restless and kept them busy from morning till night.

qb.q: How did the scientist feel about his work at Thumba Space Centre?
qb.a: The scientist felt restless because there was so much work. Despite this, he was happy to work under his boss and never thought of quitting his job.

qb.q: Why did the scientist ask his boss for permission to leave early?
qb.a: He asked for permission to leave early because he had promised to take his children to an exhibition in town.

qb.q: What happened when the scientist looked at the time after his work was completed?
qb.a: He realised that it was already half past eight in the evening. He had missed his planned time to leave and found that his boss was no longer in the office.

qb.q: How did the scientist feel about disappointing his children?
qb.a: The scientist felt sad and guilty about disappointing his children, as he had promised to take them to the exhibition, but he got caught up in his work.

qb.q: What did the wife of the scientist do when he arrived home late?
qb.a: She was calm. She did not scold him. Instead, she offered him a cup of coffee and asked if he was hungry.

qb.q: What does the passage suggest about the leadership qualities of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
qb.a: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam showed kindness, understanding and consideration for his team’s personal lives. He recognised the scientist’s commitment to work and made sure the children did not miss the exhibition.

qb.q: How did the boss help the scientist in a difficult situation?
qb.a: The boss took the children to the exhibition himself, because he saw that the scientist was too busy working and had missed the planned time to leave.

qb.q: How did the scientist’s boss show empathy towards the scientist’s situation?
qb.a: The boss understood that the scientist was too busy working to leave on time. Instead of being strict, he took the children to the exhibition himself so that they could enjoy their day.

qb.q: How did the scientist feel when he realised his boss had taken the children to the exhibition?
qb.a: He felt relieved and grateful, because he had feared disappointing his children.

qb.q: Describe the scientist’s character as depicted in the passage.
qb.a: The scientist is dedicated and hardworking, fully immersed in his work at Thumba Space Centre. Despite the heavy workload and stress, he enjoys working under his boss and never thinks of quitting. He is also a responsible father who promises to take his children to the exhibition, but gets caught up in his work. His guilt for disappointing his children reveals his caring and responsible nature.

qb.q: How does the scientist’s wife show understanding and support in the passage?
qb.a: The scientist’s wife is calm, understanding and supportive. When her husband arrives home late, expecting her to be angry, she surprises him by offering coffee and asking if he is hungry. She does not scold him but remains composed, knowing that his work is demanding.

qb.q: What qualities of leadership does Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam display in the passage?
qb.a: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is a caring and empathetic leader who understands the pressures his scientists face. When the scientist cannot take his children to the exhibition, the boss takes the initiative to do so, showing his kindness, empathy and leadership by putting the children’s needs first.

qb.q: Write a short note on the scientist’s dedication to work: How does the scientist’s dedication to his work affect his personal life?
qb.a: The scientist is dedicated and works long hours at Thumba Space Centre, often from morning till night. This commitment affects his personal life, as he loses track of time and forgets his promise to take his children to the exhibition. He feels guilty, which shows both his dedication and the challenge of balancing work and family.

qb.q: Write a short note on the boss’s thoughtfulness.
qb.a: The boss understands the scientist’s dedication to work. When he sees that the scientist is too busy to leave on time for his children, he takes the children to the exhibition himself. This shows the boss’s empathy, leadership and his concern for his team’s personal well-being.

qb.q: How does the poem describe the relationship between belief and personal strength?
qb.a: The poem suggests that belief in strength, courage and honour gives people the inner power to face challenges and prevail. Believing in oneself leads to personal growth and success.

qb.q: What does the poem suggest about the uniqueness of individuals? Explain how this idea is portrayed.
qb.a: The poem says that no matter who you are or where you are from, everyone is unique. This encourages self-acceptance and appreciation of individuality, since every person has something special to offer.

qb.q: How does the poem emphasise the power of believing in yourself? Give an example from the poem.
qb.a: The poem says, “as long as you believe in yourself, anything is possible.” This shows that self-belief is the key to overcoming obstacles and achieving dreams.

qb.q: What role do cultural expressions like song and dance play in the poem?
qb.a: Song and dance are forms of expression that reflect culture and individuality. They celebrate life and help people stay connected to their heritage and identity.

qb.q: How does the poem connect the idea of time with the concept of forever?
qb.a: The poem encourages belief in Time and Forever, suggesting that time is a continuous journey. By believing in it, people can face the future with hope and perseverance, knowing that lasting impact comes over time.

qb.q: In what way does the poem suggest that everyone has the power to be good?
qb.a: The poem says everyone has the ability to be good at heart. This means inner kindness and the power to bring positive change through good intentions.

qb.q: How does the poem suggest individuals can overcome challenges?
qb.a: By believing in strength, courage and honour, and in their own ability, individuals can overcome obstacles and succeed.

qb.q: How does the poem portray the importance of self-belief in relation to others?
qb.a: The poem encourages self-belief, and it also implies that believing in others is essential for mutual respect and support. By believing in each other, people can create positive change together.

qb.q: Explain the significance of believing in Love, Faith and Truth in the poem. How do these beliefs affect an individual’s life?
qb.a: Love, Faith and Truth are foundational virtues that guide a person’s actions and decisions. Love fosters compassion, Faith gives hope and trust in the future, and Truth encourages honesty and integrity. Together they form a strong moral compass that helps people face challenges with confidence and compassion.

qb.q: What is the relationship between belief and inner strength in the poem? Give examples from the text.
qb.a: The poem connects belief with inner strength. Believing in strength, courage and honour helps people face challenges bravely. Belief in yourself and your ability to prevail empowers you to push forward, whatever the obstacles, and turns difficulties into opportunities for growth.

qb.q: In what ways does the poem convey the importance of self-belief?
qb.a: The poem says, “as long as you believe in yourself, anything is possible.” Self-belief gives people the confidence to pursue their goals and overcome challenges. The poem encourages readers to trust their inherent qualities and strengths, which help them reach their dreams and get through life’s difficulties.

qb.q: The poem mentions ‘Believe in Time’ and ‘Believe in Forever’. How do these concepts add to the overall message of the poem?
qb.a: These phrases show that patience and perseverance are important. Time reflects growth and change, and Forever stands for lasting impact and enduring hope. The poem teaches readers to trust that their efforts will pay off over time, and to value patience and a long-term outlook.

qb.q: How does the poem highlight the uniqueness of individuals, and why is this important in the context of the poem’s message?
qb.a: The poem says everyone is unique, regardless of background, which encourages self-acceptance and individuality. Each person has something special to offer the world. This reinforces the message of self-worth and empowers people to embrace their differences and feel proud of what makes them stand out.

qb.q: Discuss the role of cultural expressions like Song and Dance in the poem. Why are they included, and what do they represent?
qb.a: Song and Dance are included to highlight the importance of cultural expression and personal creativity. They represent joy, celebration and shared human experience. Believing in Song, Dance and Culture helps people connect with their heritage, express their emotions and inspire others.

qb.q: What does the poem suggest about the connection between belief and personal growth? Give examples from the text.
qb.a: The poem suggests that belief is a catalyst for personal growth. Believing in Courage, Honour and Truth motivates people to grow. The line “Believe that no matter what happens, you have the power to prevail” shows that belief in yourself helps you overcome challenges and build resilience.

qb.q: Describe the central theme of the poem. How does the poet use various beliefs to convey this theme?
qb.a: ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. ಸೂಚನೆ: ಪ್ರೀತಿ, ನಂಬಿಕೆ, ಸತ್ಯ, ಶಕ್ತಿ, ಧೈರ್ಯ – ವೈಯಕ್ತಿಕ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ, ಸ್ಥೈರ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಅಡೆತಡೆಗಳನ್ನು ಜಯಿಸುವುದು.

qb.q: How does the poem’s theme of belief in oneself relate to the journey of personal development?
qb.a: ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. ಸೂಚನೆ: ಶಕ್ತಿ, ಧೈರ್ಯ, ಗೌರವ ಎಂಬ ಗುಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ನಂಬಿಕೆ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಿಯ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಗೆ ಹೇಗೆ ಸಹಾಯ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸ್ವವಿಶ್ವಾಸದ ಮಹತ್ವ.

qb.q: What role does the theme of uniqueness play in the poem? How does the poet encourage readers to embrace their individuality?
qb.a: ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. ಸೂಚನೆ: ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಬ್ಬರ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟತೆ, ಸ್ವೀಕಾರ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಬ್ಬರೂ ಜಗತ್ತಿಗೆ ಕೊಡುಗೆ ನೀಡಬಲ್ಲರು ಎಂಬ ಅಂಶ.
